_about: Te reo Māori names for the guide's sections, Vote sub-pages and common election labels, with the source for every term. 'official' = the Electoral Commission uses this exact term in its own te reo Māori material (quoted in 'evidence'); 'adapted' = built only from Commission wording (for example dropping words from a Commission phrase); 'dictionary' = Te Aka Māori Dictionary entry (two of them cite the Commission); 'flagged' = no established term found in the sources we could reach, so the English stays and 'mi' is null. Nothing here was made up: where we were unsure we left the English. Display rule in the app: te reo first, then English, joined by ' · '; a null 'mi' shows the English only. Checked 24 October 2026. Not checked by a fluent speaker: corrections welcome.

terms.note: No fixed term for a 'Today' page in the Commission's te reo material; Te Aka lists several words for 'today' (nōnāianei, āianei, ināianei) but none as a heading. Left in English until a fluent speaker chooses.

terms.evidence: 'Me pēwhea te pōti' (How do you vote?); 'pōti' is used throughout for vote / to vote.
Te Aka: kōwhiri '(verb) to select, pick, choose, elect'. The Commission uses kōwhiri / kōwhiringa for choosing a roll, party or candidate ('ka kōwhiri koe i te rārangi pōti').
'Ko tō pōti ā-rōpū me tuku ki te rōpū tōrangapū e tautoko nei koe' (Your party vote is for the political party…). Te Aka: rōpū tōrangapū 'political party'.

The Commission uses tūru for an electorate seat: 'ka pōti koe ki tētahi kaitono e whai ana i tētahi tūru rohe pōti whānui' (you'll vote for a candidate in a general electorate). Te Aka: tūru 'seat'. 'Ngā tūru' (the seats) is the plural; the section also covers polls and results.
From the Commission's title 'Kia rite ki te rēhita me te pōti' (Get ready to enrol and vote), dropping 'te rēhita me' (enrol and).
'Tirohia tō rohe pōti' = 'Check your electorate' (bilingual flyer).

terms.note: No Commission wording for a voting plan. Te Aka has mahere 'plan', but we have not composed a phrase; English kept.

terms.evidence: Te Aka: pōti whirirua '(noun) mixed member proportional representation, MMP', with an example sentence credited to the Electoral Commission. The te reo heading names MMP itself, not 'how it works'.
Te Aka: kuputaka '(noun) glossary'.
'Ka kīia tēnei he ‘pōti motuhake’' = 'This is known as a ‘special vote’'.
'ngā rohe pōti whānui e 64, me ngā rohe pōti Māori e 7' = '64 general electorates and 7 Māori electorates'.
From 'Kei vote.nz ētahi mōhiohio mō te rēhita me te pōti i reo kē atu' = 'Information about enrolling and voting is available in multiple languages … at vote.nz'. Te Aka: reo kē 'foreign language'.
'E rua ō pōti — he pōti ā-rōpū, he pōti ā-rohe hoki' = 'You get two votes — a party vote and an electorate vote'. Te Aka also lists 'pōti ā-pāti'; we follow the Commission.
As above; Te Aka: pōti ā-rohe 'electoral vote'.
'Kia tōmua te rēhita' = 'Enrol early'; 'Rēhitatia, tirohia, whakahoungia rānei ō taipitopito' = 'Enrol, check or update your details'.
'I te rangi pōtitanga, ka tuwhera ngā wāhi pōti i te 9am ki te 7pm' (On election day, voting places are open from 9am to 7pm).
'13 ngā rā i mua i te Rangi Pōtitanga' = '13 days before election day'. The 2025 by-election pack uses 'te rā o te pōtitanga'.
'ngā wāhi pōti tōmua' = 'advance voting places' (2025 bilingual by-election pack).
'Tirohia ngā otinga o ngā pōtitake o mua' (see the results of past referendums). Te Aka: otinga '(noun) result'. We could not reach electionresults.govt.nz to check its own wording.
'Ka kīia tēnei he ‘pōti motuhake’'; flyer: 'ka mate pea koe ki te pōti mā te pōti motuhake' (you may need to cast a special vote).
'ki te Pāremata' = 'in Parliament' (flyer). Te Aka: pāremata.
'te kaitono e hiahia ana koe kia tū hei mema Pāremata (MP)' = 'the candidate you would like to be the member of Parliament'. Te Aka: Mema Pāremata.
'ngā kaitono ā-rohe katoa' = 'the electorate candidates'. Te Aka: kaitono 'candidate (applicant)'.

terms.note: Not found in the Commission's te reo pages or Te Aka, and parliament.nz/mi could not be reached. English kept.

page_mi._about: The #/vote/lang/mi page. Every te reo Māori sentence and heading here is quoted from the Electoral Commission (source key in "source"), with the Commission’s own English counterpart. Nothing is our translation.

title.mi: Te pōti ki te Pōtitanga Whānui 2026

h.mi: Me rēhita rawa i mua i te tīmatanga o te wā pōti
h.en: You must be enrolled before voting starts

mi: Mō te Pōtitanga Whānui 2026, kāore e whakaaetia ana kia rēhita mai, kia whakahoutia rānei ō taipitopito rēhita i muri i te weherua pō o te Hanarei, te 25 o Oketopa, 2026.
en: For the 2026 General Election you can’t enrol to vote or update your enrolment details after midnight, Sunday 25 October 2026.

h.mi: Ko te rēhita hei kaipōti mēnā he Māori koe
h.en: Enrolling to vote if you are Māori

mi: Ahakoa te rārangi kaipōti e noho nei koe, kotahi tonu te rārangi rōpū tōrangapū hei kōwhiringa māu.
en: You can vote for the same list of political parties, whichever roll you’re on.

mi: Ka whakahaeretia te Pōtitanga Whānui 2026 hei te Hatarei, te 7 o Noema, 2026.
Kati ai te wā pōti hei te 7pm o te rangi pōtitanga, nā reira he roa te wā kia pōti ai koe.
en: The 2026 General Election will be held on Saturday 7 November, 2026.
Voting ends at 7pm on election day, so you’ve got plenty of time to vote.

h.mi: Me haere ki hea ki te pōti?
h.en: Where do you go to vote?

mi: Ka tere ake te pōti ina pōti koe i te rohe e noho nā koe. Heoi anō, mēnā kei wāhi kē koe, e pai tonu ana tō pōti i te wāhi pōti e pātata katoa ana ki a koe.
en: Voting is quicker if you vote in the area where you live. However, if you’re away from where you usually live, you can vote at the nearest voting place.

h.mi: He aha hei kawe atu māu ki te wāhi pōti?
h.en: What do you take with you when you vote?

mi: Kawea tō kāri PōtiMārire. Mēnā kāore anō tō kāri PōtiMārire kia tae ki a koe, i warewaretia rānei, kei te whakaae tonu tō pōti.
Kāore he take o te kawe tautohunga.
en: Take your EasyVote card with you when you vote. If you haven’t got a card or forget it, you can still vote.
You don’t need to take ID.

mi: E rua ō pōti — he pōti ā-rōpū, he pōti ā-rohe hoki.
Ka āhei tō pōti ki tētahi rōpū me tētahi kaitono, ki tētahi rānei o ērā, kaua ki tērā atu — kei a koe te tikanga.
en: You get two votes — a party vote and an electorate vote.
You can vote for a party and a candidate, or vote for only one or the other — it’s your choice.

h.mi: Mā te pōti motuhake kē pea koe e pōti ai
h.en: You may need to cast a special vote

mi: Mēnā kāore tō ingoa i te tānga rārangi kaipōti i te wāhi pōti, me mātua whakaoti e koe tētahi puka ‘special declaration vote’ i mua i tō pōti. Ka kīia tēnei he ‘pōti motuhake’.
en: If your name is not on the printed roll at a voting place, you’ll need to fill out a ‘special declaration vote’ form before you can vote. This is known as a ‘special vote’.

h.mi: Ki te hia āwhina kia pānui, kia whaitohu rānei i tō puka pōti
h.en: If you need help to read or mark your voting paper

mi: Ka āhei tētahi hoa, tētahi whanaunga, tētahi kaimahi rānei i te wāhi pōti ki te āwhina i a koe kia whaitohu i tō puka pōti.
en: A friend, family member or someone working at the voting place can help you mark your voting paper.
